item.title: Seasonal wetting and drying dynamics drive greenhouse gas emissions across Australia’s river network
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 14 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04135-1

Australian rivers emit 48.5 teragrams of carbon dioxide and 0.28 teragrams of methane annually, with dry riverbeds adding 13.9 teragrams of carbon dioxide, according to integrated river emission measurements and geospatial drainage network analysis.
item.dc:title: Seasonal wetting and drying dynamics drive greenhouse gas emissions across Australia’s river network

item.title: Geochemical clustering reveals cryptic eruptions and tephra correlations from Antarctic fumarolic ice-cave archives
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 14 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04105-7

The identification of previously unrecognised eruptions and improved correlations between ice cave deposits and other volcanic archives refine the eruptive history of Mount Melbourne, according to geochemical analyses and statistical clustering of tephra from three Antarctic ice caves with existing volcanic records.
item.dc:title: Geochemical clustering reveals cryptic eruptions and tephra correlations from Antarctic fumarolic ice-cave archives

item.title: Weathering-derived calcium supports carbon storage in grassland soils
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 13 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04142-2

Mineral weathering-derived calcium promotes soil organic carbon storage in US Mollisols, and agriculture has increased calcium inputs four- to fivefold, altering the geochemical conditions that sustain carbon in these soils, based on continental-scale datasets and geochemical modelling.
item.dc:title: Weathering-derived calcium supports carbon storage in grassland soils

item.title: Impact-based flood-damage assessment in Japan under longitudinal typhoon-track perturbations and levee-height variations during Hagibis (2019)
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 13 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04077-8

The typhoon Hagibis (2019) flood damage was highly influenced by typhoon track variations and levee height, with the highest losses concentrated around Tokyo, Osaka, and Nagoya under different storm scenarios, according to a methodological framework for assessing typhoon-induced flooding and impact analysis.
item.dc:title: Impact-based flood-damage assessment in Japan under longitudinal typhoon-track perturbations and levee-height variations during Hagibis (2019)

item.title: Ocean thermal inertia sustains a tropical Pacific mean state shift under net zero
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 13 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04082-x

The tropical Pacific shifts towards El Niño-like conditions under ongoing warming and does not recover for centuries after emissions cease, according to climate model simulations spanning centennial to millennial timescales.
item.dc:title: Ocean thermal inertia sustains a tropical Pacific mean state shift under net zero

item.title: U.S. oil and gas methane emission intensity declined 2019–2024 with little indication of federal policy impact
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 13 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04039-0

Oil and gas emissions in the USA have declined from 2019 to 2024, likely as a result of gradual technological and operational developments, and existing federal regulations, according to an inverse model constrained by satellite observations.
item.dc:title: U.S. oil and gas methane emission intensity declined 2019–2024 with little indication of federal policy impact
